sourceVerifiedFinding.question: does the upstream row carry a tenant field mapRealPermitRecord could compare pack.cityKey against?
sourceVerifiedFinding.answer: no. Read live (read-only, smartcity-os ABSOLUTE NO-TOUCH honored): server/routes/mygov.ts's /api/platform/mygov/permits hardcodes `eq(mygovPermits.tenantId, await getBastropTenantId())` server-side and accepts no caller tenant param; dbPermitToApi (the exact shape it returns) drops tenantId from its output entirely (lines 131-160, no tenant/city/jurisdiction field of any kind). This is the literal 'if the upstream response carries no tenant field to compare against, that is the finding' branch the dispatch named.
sourceVerifiedFinding.whatWouldHaveToChangeUpstream: dbPermitToApi would need to surface the row's own tenantId (or a public-safe derived city identifier) so a caller-side check could compare the RECORD's tenant, not just the feed's known-good default. Not done -- smartcity-os is no-touch.

defect2.theRealReachableGapClosedInstead: platformGrantForKind gates this feed on a pack merely HOLDING a {kind:'mygov'} object in grantedAdapters. PLATFORM_MYGOV_PERMITS_GRANT (adapters.mjs) is one city-agnostic constant currently wired only to BASTROP_TX in the static pack definitions, BUT a DB-backed pack's grantedAdapters comes straight off a `granted_adapters` column (city-pack.mjs line ~241) -- settable by an ordinary row write, no code review, no deploy. Nothing before this fix stopped a second pack from acquiring that exact grant object and reaching mapRealPermitRecord, which would then fetch Bastrop's real permits (the only tenant the hardcoded query serves) and stamp them with that OTHER pack's cityKey.
defect2.fix: assertVerifiedMygovTenant(cityKey) in src/mygov-permits.mjs refuses (throws) unless cityKey === 'bastrop_tx', the one tenant the hardcoded upstream query is verified to serve. Guarded twice through the one shared function: composeRealPermits (before the network call, so a mis-granted pack doesn't spend the platform key) and mapRealPermitRecord itself (the function this mission named).
defect2.falsifier: If composeRealPermits or mapRealPermitRecord returned/stamped a record for any cityKey other than 'bastrop_tx' without throwing, the fix would be contradicted.
defect2.contradicted: no -- 5 new tests confirm: the constant matches what smartcity-os actually hardcodes; the guard passes bastrop_tx and is not vacuous; it refuses template-city, icc-demo, empty string, null, and undefined; mapRealPermitRecord throws on a cross-tenant stamp attempt using a real sample row; composeRealPermits throws BEFORE fetchImpl is ever invoked (verified via a call-tracking spy).

violationTestBothDirections.violationRefused: mapRealPermitRecord(SAMPLE_ROW, 'template-city', ...) throws /mygov real feed is verified live for bastrop_tx only/; composeRealPermits(TEMPLATE_CITY, ...) rejects with the same message and fetchCalled stays false
violationTestBothDirections.legitimateCaseSucceeds: composeRealPermits(BASTROP_TX, ...) and mapRealPermitRecord(row, 'bastrop_tx', ...) both proceed exactly as before -- unchanged by the guard, confirmed by all 11 pre-existing tests in mygov-permits.test.mjs still passing

defect2.whyNoLiveHttpRepro: No pack other than bastrop_tx holds the mygov grant today, so there is no live cross-tenant call to reproduce a leak against over HTTP -- that absence IS the 'coincidental, not enforced' framing this mission's preamble uses. The unit-level violation test is the correct fidelity, matching how the fixture side's own paired control (domains.test.mjs, 'returned a record for other-city on pack probe-city') is unit-level too, not an HTTP demonstration.
